Build a configurator#

Let a buyer choose the fabric, the legs and the size — on the real scene, in a frame, with the price updating and a link that opens exactly what they picked. The scene stays one upload; the choices are a schema you author in Studio.

You need: a Studio account, a streamed scene you own (ingest/<id>.vpk), and a model whose variations are either KHR_materials_variants (what Blender / Substance / most DCC exporters write) or simply extra materials you can point at.

1. Prepare the model#

Two ways to express a choice, mix freely:

  • Material variants. Author KHR_materials_variants in the file (in Blender: the Material Variants panel). The compiler carries the table into the scene; each variant name becomes something an option can apply. A variant may swap several materials at once — that is one option.
  • Extra materials. Give the alternative look its own material on a hidden or duplicate primitive, or just leave it unused in the file. An option can then say material 4 draws as material 7 (materials: {"4": 7}), in any combination — multi-material groups without touching the exporter.
  • Show / hide. An option can black out materials (hide: [4]) — "no armrest", "without the canopy". Honest limit today: the surface turns black rather than disappearing (the engine has no per-material hide lane yet; the hidden mask from the BIM work replaces it).

Material indices are the glTF order; Studio shows them with names next to the fields.

2. Author the groups in Studio#

Open /studio, find the scene card and press Configurator.

  1. Add group — name it ("Fabric").
  2. + option per choice — name it ("Walnut"), pick the variant it applies from the dropdown and/or type aliases (4→7, 5→7) and/or the materials to black out (4, 5). Add a SKU and a price if you want the panel to total them (the price is a label — Verse never bills anyone).
  3. The first option of each group is the default. Set a currency and a base price at the top if you want a running total.
  4. Save configurator, then Try it in the viewer.

Everything is validated on save with the same code the viewer renders with; a variant name that is not in the scene is dropped with a warning rather than saved broken. Prefer the API? It is one call:

Code
curl -sS -X PUT https://HOST/v1/scenes/SCENE/config -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "currency": "USD", "base": 890,
  "groups": [
    { "name": "Fabric", "options": [
      { "name": "Oak",    "variant": "Oak" },
      { "name": "Walnut", "variant": "Walnut", "price": 120, "sku": "SOFA-WAL" } ] },
    { "name": "Legs", "options": [
      { "name": "Steel", "materials": { "4": 7 } },
      { "name": "None",  "hide": [4], "price": -40 } ] } ] }'

Ids are slugged from the names (fabric, walnut); set your own ids when they must stay stable across renames.

3. What visitors get#

A Configure chip in the toolbar opens the panel: one row of chips per group, a swatch from the material it applies, the option's price, and the total at the bottom. Every pick changes the scene in a frame — no re-stream — and rewrites the link:

Code
https://HOST/?vpk=ingest/<id>.vpk&cfg=fabric:walnut,legs:none

Only non-default picks are in the string, so a plain link still opens the default. Send that link, put it in a quote, paste it into the CRM.

4. In your own page#

The embed SDK keeps the panel out of the iframe and gives you the data:

Code
<div id="sofa"></div>
<script src="https://HOST/embed.js"></script>
<script>
  const viewer = Verse.embed(document.getElementById("sofa"), { scene: "SCENE", cfg: { fabric: "walnut" } });
  viewer.on("configuration", (c) => {
    // c.groups: [{ id, name, default, options: [{ id, name, price?, sku?, swatch? }] }]
    renderYourSwatches(c.groups, c.selection);
    total.textContent = c.priced ? `${c.total} ${c.currency}` : "";
    addToQuote.dataset.skus = c.skus.join("+");
    share.href = `https://HOST/?vpk=ingest/SCENE.vpk&cfg=${c.cfg}`;
  });
  fabricSelect.onchange = () => viewer.setConfiguration({ fabric: fabricSelect.value });
</script>

getConfiguration() returns the same shape on demand. TypeScript users get VerseConfiguration from verse-embed.d.ts; server-side, @ctruhtech/verse-sdk has scenes.config(id), scenes.setConfig(id, schema) and shareLink(id, { cfg }).

5. Hear about changes#

Add a webhook in Studio (Webhooks, bottom of the library) with the config.changed event and your endpoint receives a signed POST whenever the schema is saved — handy for keeping a product catalogue in step. See docs/api.md § Webhooks for the signature recipe.

Limits#

  • 16 groups × 32 options; a later group wins a material conflict.
  • Visibility is a black-out, per material (see above).
  • Prices and SKUs are display only; checkout is yours.
  • Classic (non-compiled .glb) scenes have no schema — compile them.
